title: Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances (FR Doc. 2026-22192)
key_claim: HHS does not intend to take enforcement action against state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities or licensed physicians compounding listed peptide bulk drug substances while the 503A bulks list is developed through rulemaking; it may revisit the policy if a safety signal or product quality issue arises; it cites significant interest given the lack of approved products; comments were open for 2 weeks after publication.
frame_summary: HHS frames the policy as a temporary, conditional measure to expand patient access to peptides while formal rulemaking proceeds.

title: Comments to HHS on Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Peptide Compounding
key_claim: The center-right institute asks HHS to withdraw the policy until FDA completes individual safety and efficacy assessments, or else set a fixed expiration date; it notes Enhanced began offering all six peptides through its telehealth platform and warns the policy risks encouraging a less burdensome distribution model than clinical trials.

title: The FDA Should Not Allow Untested Peptides to Be Added Into Patients' Medications
key_claim: Ahead of the July 2026 Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee, four of the seven peptides under discussion had no human safety studies at all, and FDA's own scientists recommended against listing all of them. The peptides under discussion were described as manufactured by Chinese firms.
frame_summary: ITIF argues that compounding untested peptides bypasses the evidence the FDA's own scientists said was missing.

title: HHS will permit compounding of six peptides ahead of formal rulemaking
key_claim: The six peptides are BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax and TB-500, proposed for uses including wound healing, osteoporosis, obesity, insomnia and inflammatory conditions; the policy targets research-use-only peptides from foreign manufacturers; Public Citizen urged that all peptides go through standard FDA approval.
frame_summary: RAPS reports the policy as a regulatory shortcut ahead of rulemaking, setting HHS's gray-market rationale against critics who say it undermines approval.

title: AMA opposes HHS proposal to expand access to unapproved peptides
key_claim: None of the six peptides is FDA-approved and none is under review in an active Investigational New Drug application; the AMA urges HHS to rescind the policy and require FDA review including clinical trials.
frame_summary: The AMA argues the policy bypasses science and turns patients into test subjects, and that only the approval route can establish safety.

title: The PEPTIDE-L Wave Reaches HHS: Enforcement Discretion ... Not the Finish Line
key_claim: The policy is conditional enforcement discretion while rulemaking proceeds, not final placement on the 503A bulks list; after 15 years, only six bulk substances have been moved from the interim list through rulemaking; routes are restricted by peptide.
frame_summary: The law firm argues the policy is a conditional interim pathway rather than a green light, and that the rulemaking it waits on has historically moved very slowly.
